metadata.title: Pressure Fundamentals
metadata.topic: Pressure as force distributed over area

learningPurpose: Give students a focused, source-gated reference for the pressure relationship used in the first fluid-pressure lesson.

definitions.meaning: Force distributed normally over a stated area for the introductory training case.

governingPrinciples: Use SI units internally: pascal for pressure, newton for force, and square metre for area.
The introductory relationship applies only when the force and area are stated and the force is normal to the area.
This file is blocked from approval until a real fluid-mechanics source is onboarded.
assumptions: Force is normal to the surface.
The training case does not model dynamic pressure or equipment design.
limitations: Does not cover compressibility, dynamic flow, pressure-vessel rules, pressure ratings, or safety procedures.
No approved source section or page range is available yet.

workedExample.title: Pressure from stated force and area
workedExample.purpose: Show the SI relationship without adding unreviewed manufacturer or standards information.

normalOperation: The calculation is acceptable for the training case only after units and source evidence are checked.
commonMisconceptions: Treating pressure as the same quantity as force.
Using area in cm^2 without an explicit conversion step.
Applying the classroom equation to real pressurised equipment without safety approval.

faultConditions.title: Incorrect area unit
symptoms: The calculated pressure is off by orders of magnitude.
likelyCauses: Area was entered in cm^2 or mm^2 as if it were m^2.
faultConditions.safeResponse: Stop the calculation, identify the unit, and perform only an explicit reviewed conversion.

safety.warning: Introductory pressure calculations do not authorise work on real pressurised systems.
safety.studentBoundary: Students must use approved training examples or supervised laboratory procedures.
